issues.detail: server_derived_reject rejects whenever /trusted/customerDisabled EXISTS regardless of value. It is designed to forbid client submission of server-owned fields, not to test a boolean state. This rule rejects Sales Order creation even when customerDisabled is false, so the documented disabled-customer condition is not implemented.

The path /trusted/customerDisabled is a server_state boolean, not a client-submitted field. Using server_derived_reject on it adds an unsupported constraint semantics: unconditional rejection on presence rather than a value-based disabled check.

judge.reason: Candidate A misuses server_derived_reject to check a trusted boolean. Per operator semantics this primitive rejects on path existence regardless of value and is not a boolean-state permission test. The source (VIS-FSV-B17-01) says disallowing sales orders happens when the customer is Disabled, i.e., a value-dependent check. The rule would reject all Sales Order creation whenever the trusted path is present, including when customerDisabled is false, so the target is not implemented and an unsupported constraint is introduced.

The path is a declared server_state boolean (VIS-FSV-B17-RUNTIME-ABI). on_missing deny aligns with the default missing-input rejection semantics. No unsupported constraints are added; scope is limited to the disabled-customer condition for the target operation.

judge.reason: Candidate A implements the supplier hold policy for Purchase Order creation. The bounded_guard_dnf ALLOW alternatives are: supplier not on hold, or holdType equals Payments. This matches the source: Invoices and All hold types block Purchase Orders, while Payments does not. Declared trusted paths /trusted/supplierOnHold and /trusted/holdType are used, and on_missing=deny satisfies the missing-input rejection requirement. No unsupported extra constraints or direction issues are visible.

objective.constraint_object: Supplier on-hold status and hold type relevant to Purchase Order creation
objective.constraint_kind: The documented supplier hold-type condition for the target operation
objective.scope: Implement the supplier hold policy for this Purchase Order target only; do not add restrictions for invoices, payments, other endpoints or unrelated fields.

snapshot_content_lines.text: The hold types are as follows:

+ Invoices: ERPNext will not allow Purchase Invoices or Purchase Orders to be created for the supplier + Payments: ERPNext will not allow Payment Entries to be created for the Supplier + All: ERPNext will apply both hold types aboveIf you do not set a release date, ERPNext will hold the Supplier **indefinitely**.

issues.detail: The ALLOW alternatives require supplierOnHold=true and holdType in {Invoices, All}. Source says Invoices and All block Purchase Orders, so these are exactly the conditions that should deny, not allow. The rule is inverted.
on_missing is set to skip, but the operation does not explicitly support skip. Missing trusted inputs should reject per declared semantics.

judge.reason: Candidate B inverts the hold-type semantics: it allows Purchase Order creation when supplierOnHold is true and holdType is Invoices or All, which source evidence states should block Purchase Orders. It also uses on_missing=skip despite no explicit skip support, contrary to the missing-input rejection requirement.
